briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Storefronts Multiply, Wall Street Circles: Momentum Builds From Washtenaw County to the DEA
briefs.top: Michigan's retail map keeps expanding even as the 24% wholesale tax fight spills into the governor's race, with new Ann Arbor-area storefronts opening and GOP frontrunner John James making repeal a campaign plank. Nationally, institutional capital is lining up for a Schedule III world, Curaleaf just sweetened its Aurora bid, and Compass Pathways is closing in on an FDA filing for its psilocybin drug.

local.text: Cloud Cannabis opens new Ann Arbor storefront Oct. 19 — The Michigan-based chain, co-founded by a former Detroit police officer, is opening at 1760 Plymouth Rd. with curbside service and a 'patients-over-profit' model for both medical and rec customers.
Bloom City Club expands into Ypsilanti with new store — The Ann Arbor-based retailer is marking the opening with a full slate of cannabis-themed events throughout October.

Menominee could add four more dispensaries via ballot measure — A citizen petition drive would raise the city's store cap from nine to thirteen, and organizers say they gathered more than enough signatures to put it before voters in November.

Governor's race gives operators a real shot at tax relief — GOP frontrunner John James has made repealing or reducing the 24% wholesale tax a core campaign plank, after earning the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's endorsement over his opposition to the levy.

Regulators clear bad actors, clean the path for compliant brands — The state revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a company $2 million for shipping 'dirt and mulch' labeled as marijuana, pulled Muha Meds' Ypsilanti license over illegal influencer sales, and Bay City is reinvesting weed tax dollars into a homeless shelter.

national.text: Wall Street capital is lining up for Schedule III cannabis — Institutional investors are preparing for an influx of capital once rescheduling lands, a shift that could unlock billions in funding for an industry generating $30 billion in annual sales.

Curaleaf sweetens hostile Aurora Cannabis bid by 25% — The MSO raised its offer to roughly $5 per share in cash-and-stock, bumped its cap price to $6, and extended the takeover window through December 4.

Compass Pathways nears first-ever psychedelic FDA filing — The company plans to submit its rolling New Drug Application for psilocybin treatment COMP360 between October and December, with fresh Phase 3 data presented this month at the ASCP Annual Meeting showing durable relief for treatment-resistant depression.

DEA rescheduling pause is procedural, not a rejection — A federal judge's stay over a new GAO report hits its key response deadline today, Oct. 13, but the delay only affects broader adult-use rescheduling — FDA-approved and state-medical marijuana products were already moved to Schedule III in April.

States gear up for Schedule III, demand DEA guidance — A growing number of state marijuana regulators are pressing federal officials for clarity on implementing the Trump administration's rescheduling move, signaling states are actively preparing for the shift rather than waiting it out.
